method: Read all 19 assigned target/context bodies in full from preserved HTML; checked XML dates and people, exclusions, footnotes, annotations, enclosures, scholarly material and bibliographies. Compared Darwin targets backward against Susan’s incoming texts, distinguishing receipt, reading, forwarding, family relay and prospective requests. No direct or reverse link was proposed from shared family subject matter alone.

outgoing_reviews.title: To Susan Darwin 14 July – 7 August [1832]
outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin’s multipart July–August letter describes the first voyage plans, Rio and Monte Video, projected routes, shipboard routine, collecting and finances, a delayed specimen box, and an August update about Buenos Aires unrest and the Rio Negro departure. The dated additions are distinct sections; the body says he expects an answer to a Bahia letter, but does not identify that input.
outgoing_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

outgoing_reviews.title: To Susan Darwin 3 December [1833]
outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Susan to tell their father about a £17 bill and reports the projected Tierra del Fuego winter, route, fossil bones, sea-sickness and expected letter opportunity at the Falklands. It is a self-contained outgoing update with no identified Susan prompt.
outgoing_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

outgoing_reviews.title: To Susan Darwin 23 April 1835
outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin explicitly received Susan’s November letter, then gives a long account of his Mendoza/Cordillera expedition, geological theories, red snow, final cargo and finances, and asks family members to remember others. The receipt is direct, but its substantive report is not a response to a distinctive question in Susan’s letter.
outgoing_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

outgoing_reviews.title: To Susan Darwin 3 [September] 1835
outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin explains a larger bill, the delayed Peruvian survey, route to Sydney and his longing for home. He notes that warships brought no letters and that the Admiral is forwarding them to Sydney; no incoming Susan text is identified as read here.
outgoing_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

outgoing_reviews.title: To Susan Darwin 28 January 1836
outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin’s January letter asks Susan to explain a bill and reports Sydney, Bathurst, absence of letters, return route and expenses. He explicitly received no letters at Sydney; the source contains no identifiable Susan prompt.
outgoing_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

outgoing_reviews.title: To Susan Darwin 4 August [1836]
outgoing_reviews.summary: Darwin explains the altered Southern Hemisphere route, reports receipt at Ascension of Catherine’s October and Susan’s November letters, and describes how news from home revived his interest in Ascension geology. The named letters are not among the assigned incoming IDs; the receipt and reading boundary is explicit.
outgoing_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

additional_compared_sources.title: To J. S. Henslow1 [c. 26 October –] 24 November [1832]
additional_compared_sources.summary: Darwin sends a cargo with specimens and fossil material, reports overland travel and collecting, asks for mineralogical books and advice, and outlines the Tierra del Fuego and Chile route. It is the November-dated outgoing letter later identified by Susan as received by the family.
additional_compared_sources.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 12 February [– 3 March] 1832
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan composes a birthday and family journal for Darwin, following the family plan of alternating monthly letters and deliberately reporting past events rather than future plans. It covers the death of Darwin’s grandmother, family marriages, local news, shells Papa asked Hughes to save, Beechey’s voyage, cholera and household events, and delayed correspondence to Rio. No distinctive Darwin prompt is recoverable.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 12 May [– 2 June] 1832
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan acknowledges Darwin’s recent St Salvador account and a second Lyra letter, circulates them to family, copies messages to Eyton and others, and reports Cambridge, family and political news. Her source is a family information relay; it does not uniquely identify a surviving Darwin letter among the assigned targets.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 15[–18] August 1832
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan says a letter to Catherine accompanied one for Mr Owen dated Rio, reports family news, commissions, illness and regular correspondence, and asks Darwin to date future letters. The referenced Darwin letters are to other recipients and their identities are not recoverable from this body.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 12–18 November 1832
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan gives family and travel news, reports that visitors read some of Darwin’s first letters, and discusses the hoped-for return and social plans. The reading of earlier letters is knowledge about Darwin’s correspondence, not a specific prompt for the assigned outgoing targets.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 3–6 March 1833
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan and the family praise Darwin’s November letter and geological discoveries, report family news, and add a March 6 note explaining that Beaufort sent the letter onward to the Buenos Aires mail. The explicit November reference and forwarding route fit Darwin 192, but the response is family news rather than a complete answer to its geology.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 22–31 July 1833
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan apologizes for missing a monthly turn, reports waiting for news from the Beagle, family visits and Cambridge reports, and mentions hearing that Darwin’s things arrived safely. It contains no uniquely identifiable Darwin letter prompt.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 15 October 1833
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan records receiving Darwin’s letter dated Maldonado 14 July and his Journal, says the Journal has only been partly read, forwards the letter to Erasmus, and arranges books and shoes. She separately asks about an Owen letter and Catherine’s September letter. This is a direct receipt and partial-reading witness for Darwin 177.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 12[–28] February 1834
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan’s multipart birthday letter records the family’s waiting for Darwin’s next account, corrects spelling in his Journal, reports domestic and political news, offers a book, and closes as she expects he has sailed for Valparaiso. The Journal corrections are a family editorial response, not a distinctive incoming letter to Darwin.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin [23] May 1834
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan explains Catherine’s words inserted into an Owen letter, forwards Darwin’s November letter to Erasmus, discusses his fossil skull and family news, and expresses longing for his return. The letter contains no distinctive request that identifies a surviving Darwin target.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin [24] November 1834
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan reports the Langtons’ packet to Madeira, family and political news, and a long extract from Erasmus’s letter about Cambridge conversations. It is a social and family journal with no Darwin prompt uniquely linked to the assigned targets.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 16 February 1835
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan worries about Darwin’s illness and the Beagle’s crowded conditions, relays FitzRoy’s promotion, discusses Erasmus’s letters and Tom Eyton’s correspondence, and reports family news. A partial letter from Erasmus is distinct from Susan’s text; no Darwin target is established.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 22 November 1835
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan confirms safe arrival of Darwin’s Journal after concern over the Challenger, says the family is reading it aloud, quotes Sedgwick’s praise from a letter to Butler, and reports family news. The quoted Sedgwick passage is third-party forwarded knowledge, not Susan’s own answer or a prompt for Darwin 294.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Susan Darwin 12 February 1836
incoming_reviews.summary: Susan sends Darwin a birthday letter, celebrates his scientific prospects, comments on his early Journal and geology, reports family news and hopes for his return and Galapagos account. The future-facing request does not identify an earlier incoming letter.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

proposed_links.scope: Susan explicitly identifies the received Maldonado 14 July letter and its partial Journal reading; this activates receipt and partial reading for that Darwin letter only.

proposed_links.scope: Susan’s March letter identifies Darwin’s November letter and forwards the family response by Beaufort; it is scoped to receipt and family reaction, not a complete answer to Darwin 192’s geology.

proposed_links.scope: Susan identifies a letter to Catherine and one to Owen dated Rio, but neither is uniquely assigned to a surviving Darwin target in this packet.

proposed_links.scope: Darwin says he received Susan’s November letter, but his geology and finance report does not identify a question answered from its body; preserve receipt without forcing a substantive reply edge.

findings: 219 is the clearest direct receipt/partial reading witness: its Maldonado 14 July date matches Darwin 177’s dated opening and it separately says the Journal had only been read a few pages.
200’s November-letter reference and Beaufort forwarding fit Darwin 192’s November-dated outgoing letter, but the family text does not answer its geological questions.
275 and 306 explicitly separate receipt of family letters from Darwin’s own later composition; the named letters are not silently substituted for other Susan records.
No assigned Susan incoming source supplies a distinctive prompt for Darwin 233, 286, 294 or 306; shared homesickness, family news and ship logistics remain negative evidence.
limitations: All 19 assigned records were read from the plan-pinned preserved HTML/XML paths and hashes.
No inline figures were present in these 19 preserved HTML pages; no figure asset was needed.
The Beagle plan is navigation evidence rather than an accepted matching ledger; unlocated family letters remain unlocated.
